newsitem.title: HONG KONG: HK activists hide cash and files from China's eyes.
newsitem.headline: HK activists hide cash and files from China's eyes.

text.p: A pro-democracy group in Hong Kong that China has labelled as subversive said on Monday it had moved its cash and sensitive files in case of trouble when Beijing resumes sovereignty over the territory in 50 days.

Cheung Man-kwong, a spokesman of the Alliance in Support of the Patriotic Democratic Movement in China, told a newspaper the group had hidden sensitive documents including files containing details about Chinese dissidents and their supporters.
"For the safety of the people involved, we have to ensure all these personal files are kept under wraps," Cheung told the South China Morning Post.

Cheung declined to say whether the files had been sent abroad, the newspaper said. The alliance had also transferred more than HK$3 million (US$387,600) cash from three banks to other accounts, it said.
Alliance officials were not available to give further details.
The alliance is the "mass movement" side of Hong Kong's pro-democracy camp, which also counts several political parties.
It grew out of spontaneous popular opposition in Hong Kong to Beijing's June 4, 1989, crackdown on pro-democracy demonstrations centred on Tiananmen Square.

The alliance has been the main organiser of big anti-Beijing protests in Hong Kong, and its activists have helped dissidents who fled from the mainland after the bloody 1989 crackdown, some of whom live in exile in Hong Kong.
The pro-democracy movement has voiced fears for the safety of its own activists and these dissidents after Britain returns Hong Kong to China at midnight on June 30.

Another Hong Kong newspaper, the mass-selling Apple Daily, said on Monday that a Chinese dissident sheltering in Hong Kong since 1991 would set himself on fire during the anniversary of the 1989 crackdown next month.
The dissident, who was not named, was quoted as saying his suicide would be a protest against the colonial government's refusal to help him settle in another country.
The alliance plans big rallies and an overnight candlelight vigil in Hong Kong on June 3-4 to honour the dead of 1989.
